title: Vael’s planets, with a scale and a growing chart (a CI fixture)
dek: An invented star with three planets on a scale and a count that grows faster than you expect (a CI fixture).

blocks.text: Vael has three planets, and the gap between them is bigger than it looks. Where would you stand?

stops.prompt: Is the farthest planet about twice as far as the nearest?
options: No, it is about ten times as far
stops.explain: Sarn sits ten times as far from Vael as Orrin does.
stops.twist: Planets in drawings are crowded together. The real gaps are far wider.
stops.simple: Sarn is about ten times as far.

blocks.text: Orrin is where you live. Zoom out to see how far the others are. Each tick on the line is ten times the one before it.
Light takes longer to reach a far planet, and it spreads over more ground on the way.

guide.line: Out here, my light is thin. Look how far it has to go.

blocks.text: Now a count. On Orrin’s ferries, doubling the crates does much more than double the trips. Step through the counts.

stops.prompt: Ten times the crates needs how many times the trips?
stops.explain: Ten times the crates takes a hundred times the trips on Orrin’s ferries.
stops.twist: Ten is the natural first guess. Each crate has to meet every other, so the work grows with the square.
stops.simple: Ten times the crates, a hundred times the trips.

blocks.text: Distances and counts both grow in steps that surprise us. Keep an eye on the scale of every number.

stops.simple: Check the scale of a number.

stops.prompt: A new planet is a hundred times Orrin’s distance. How does that sit on the line?
stops.explain: A hundred times is far beyond Sarn, which is only ten times as far.
stops.twist: Planets drawn in a row look evenly spaced, so a hundred times can seem close.
stops.simple: A hundred times is far beyond Sarn.

asides.title: Where this stops
asides.text: The planets and the ferries are invented for this fixture; real distances are not tidy numbers.

askSuggestions: What would change if the numbers were different?
Where does this picture stop being true?
